name: Isaiah
bio:
Isaiah son of Amoz was a prophet of the LORD. When Sennacherib's officer Rabshakeh threatened Jerusalem with blasphemous taunts against the LORD, Hezekiah sent his officials to Isaiah, who answered that Sennacherib would hear a rumor, withdraw, and fall by the sword in his own land — a word that came true in full (2 Kings 19:1-7, 36-37). When Sennacherib sent a second threatening letter, Hezekiah spread it before the LORD in the temple and prayed; Isaiah then sent him a detailed oracle of judgment against Sennacherib, mocking the Assyrian king's pride and promising that the LORD would defend Jerusalem for his own sake and David's, turning Sennacherib back by the way he came. That night the angel of the LORD struck down 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp (2 Kings 19:20-35).

## 📖 Core Story: Healing, a Sign, and a Warning

When Hezekiah fell fatally ill, Isaiah told him to prepare to die, but after Hezekiah's tearful prayer, the LORD sent Isaiah back with news that fifteen years would be added to his life. At Hezekiah's request for a sign, Isaiah called on the LORD, and the shadow on Ahaz's sundial moved backward ten steps instead of forward (2 Kings 20:1-11). Later, after Hezekiah proudly showed Babylonian envoys all his treasures, Isaiah confronted him and prophesied that everything would one day be carried off to Babylon, and Hezekiah's descendants would become eunuchs there — a warning Hezekiah accepted since peace would last through his own lifetime (2 Kings 20:12-19).

## 📖 Core Story: The Call of Isaiah

In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw a vision of the LORD seated on a throne high and lifted up, with seraphim crying "Holy, holy, holy" and the temple filled with smoke. Overwhelmed by his own uncleanness in God's presence, Isaiah was purified when a seraph touched his lips with a live coal from the altar; when the LORD asked who would go for him, Isaiah volunteered, and was commissioned to preach to a people who would not understand until the land lay utterly desolate, though a holy remnant would remain (Isaiah 6:1-13).

## 📖 Core Story: Signs for Ahaz and His Sons' Names

When Syria and Israel under Rezin and Pekah besieged Jerusalem, the LORD sent Isaiah and his son Shear-jashub to reassure King Ahaz that the plot would fail; Isaiah offered Ahaz a sign of his choosing, and when Ahaz refused to ask, Isaiah gave the sign of Immanuel — a child who would be born to a virgin, and before he grew old enough to choose between good and evil, both threatening kingdoms would be destroyed (Isaiah 7:1-25). Isaiah then fathered another son with symbolic significance: at the LORD's instruction, he had the prophetess conceive and bear a son named Maher-shalal-hash-baz ("the spoil speeds, the prey hastens"), witnessed by Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah, as a sign that Damascus and Samaria would fall to Assyria before the child could speak (Isaiah 8:1-4).

## 📖 Core Story: The Sign-Act of Nakedness

When Sargon king of Assyria sent his commander to capture Ashdod, the LORD had Isaiah walk around naked and barefoot for three years as a living sign that Egypt and Ethiopia, in whom Judah was tempted to trust, would likewise be led away captive and shamed by Assyria (Isaiah 20:1-6).
